themes.title: Far-right parties push 'national priority' policies
themes.blurb: Right-wing and far-right parties across Europe are intensifying their focus on 'national priority' policies, particularly in Spain, Italy, and France. This theme reflects a shared rhetorical and policy framework emphasizing national sovereignty, stricter immigration controls, and opposition to EU-driven social policies. The convergence is evident in regional elections, coalition negotiations, and public statements by party leaders.

countries.name: 🇪🇸 Vox
countries.note: Demands 'national priority' in Andalusia elections, forcing PP to negotiate policy concessions like excluding undocumented migrants from early childhood aid.

countries.name: 🇮🇹 Fratelli d'Italia / Lega
countries.note: Salvini and Meloni push for stricter immigration laws, including revoking citizenship for serious crimes, following Modena car attack.

countries.name: 🇫🇷 Rassemblement National
countries.note: Marine Le Pen and Jordan Bardella advocate for national sovereignty in economic and immigration policies, positioning RN as a mainstream alternative.

countries.name: 🇬🇧 Reform UK
countries.note: Campaigns on anti-immigration platform, gaining traction in local elections and influencing mainstream parties' policies.

themes.title: Trump’s policies dominate global right-wing coverage
themes.blurb: Donald Trump's foreign and domestic policies continue to shape right-wing discourse worldwide, with extensive coverage of his Iran strategy, trade deals with China, and domestic initiatives like voter eligibility checks. This theme highlights Trump's enduring influence on transnational right-wing narratives, particularly in the U.S., Poland, Argentina, and Italy, where his policies are either emulated or criticized by local right-wing factions.

countries.name: 🇺🇸 MAGA / Trump

countries.note: Meloni and Salvini navigate Trump’s influence, balancing support for U.S. policies with Italy’s strategic interests in the Mediterranean.

themes.title: Car attack in Modena sparks immigration debate
themes.blurb: A vehicular attack in Modena, Italy, has ignited a transnational debate on immigration, integration, and security policies. Right-wing parties in Italy, France, Spain, and the UK are leveraging the incident to advocate for stricter immigration controls, revocation of citizenship for criminals, and 'remigration' policies. The coverage reflects a shared narrative linking immigration to public safety concerns.

countries.name: 🇮🇹 Fratelli d'Italia / Lega
countries.note: Salvini and Meloni use Modena attack to push for stricter immigration laws, including revoking citizenship for serious crimes.

countries.name: 🇫🇷 Rassemblement National
countries.note: RN seizes on Modena incident to reinforce anti-immigration stance, calling for stricter integration policies and deportations.

countries.name: 🇪🇸 Vox
countries.note: Vox links Modena attack to broader immigration concerns, demanding 'national priority' policies in Andalusia.

countries.name: 🇬🇧 Reform UK
countries.note: Reform UK uses Modena incident to bolster anti-immigration platform, calling for stricter border controls and deportation policies.

themes.title: Internal divisions within far-right parties
themes.blurb: Far-right and right-wing parties in Poland, Hungary, Argentina, and Germany are grappling with internal divisions, leadership challenges, and factional infighting. These conflicts are driven by ideological differences, personal rivalries, and strategic disagreements over alliances and policy directions. The coverage highlights the fragility of right-wing coalitions and the potential for fragmentation.

countries.name: 🇭🇺 Fidesz / Tisza

countries.name: 🇦🇷 La Libertad Avanza
countries.note: Javier Milei’s government struggles with infighting, particularly between Karina Milei and Santiago Caputo, over policy and leadership.

countries.name: 🇩🇪 Alternative für Deutschland
countries.note: AfD faces internal conflicts over leadership and extremism, with factions clashing over strategy ahead of regional elections.

themes.title: Rise of far-right parties in European polls
themes.blurb: Far-right parties in Germany, Sweden, France, and Hungary are gaining significant traction in polls and elections, reflecting a broader shift toward nationalist and anti-establishment politics. This theme captures the growing electoral success of these parties, their influence on mainstream politics, and the challenges they pose to traditional center-right and center-left parties.

countries.name: 🇩🇪 Alternative für Deutschland
countries.note: AfD leads polls in Saxony-Anhalt and Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, with 28-29% support, forcing mainstream parties to adapt.

countries.name: 🇸🇪 Sverigedemokraterna
countries.note: SD gains influence in Sweden, shaping government policies on immigration and integration, despite internal divisions.

countries.name: 🇫🇷 Rassemblement National
countries.note: RN consolidates support ahead of 2027 presidential elections, with nearly 50% of French voters considering it a viable option.

countries.name: 🇭🇺 Fidesz / Tisza
countries.note: Tisza Party challenges Fidesz’s dominance, reshaping Hungary’s political landscape with a focus on anti-corruption and EU relations.
